title: Install from a Marketplace, and Author One

questions.prompt: Your plugin loads under `claude --plugin-dir ./guardrail-kit` and its skill runs, but the PreToolUse hook never fires. You run the script by hand with piped stdin and it exits 2 correctly. `claude plugin validate` passes. Where do you look next, and why?
options: Reinstall the plugin through a marketplace — `--plugin-dir` runs hooks in a sandbox where PreToolUse never fires
Check the hook debug log after triggering the event: a loaded hook whose matcher never matched looks identical to a hook that isn't loaded
Add `disable-model-invocation: false` to the hook's frontmatter so the harness schedules it
Move `hooks/hooks.json` into `.claude-plugin/` so it is discovered alongside the manifest
questions.explanation: Validate passing plus the script behaving correctly by hand narrows the failure to wiring, not logic — and the wiring check is the debug log, which reports which hooks matched, their exit codes, and their output. `--plugin-dir` loads hooks exactly as an installed plugin does (A is false). Hooks have no frontmatter and no model-invocation flag (C invents a field). Moving the file into `.claude-plugin/` is the one place hooks definitely do not load (D), and it would have broken validate, which passed.

questions.prompt: You converted your `.claude/settings.json` setup into a plugin. Skills and agents both work, so you deleted the originals from `.claude/`. Now a teammate reports every blocked git command prints its refusal twice. What is happening?
options: The plugin is installed twice, once per component directory, so each hook fires twice
You moved the hooks but left the original `hooks` block in `.claude/settings.json`, and plugin hooks carry no namespace prefix to de-duplicate them
The matcher `"Bash"` matched two tools — the shell tool and the plugin's own script runner — so each hook ran twice
Exit code 2 causes Claude Code to retry the PreToolUse check once before surfacing the block
questions.explanation: Skills and agents get a `guardrail-kit:` prefix, so the two sets coexisted harmlessly and deleting the originals was correct. Hooks get no prefix and no conflict detection — the leftover block in `settings.json` and the plugin's copy both match `PreToolUse` on `Bash`, so both run. Plugins are installed once per source, not per component directory (A), a matcher names tool types rather than counting them (C), and exit 2 blocks without retrying (D). This is the exact failure the convert-and-keep-originals order exists to prevent: verify the plugin's hooks work before deleting the old ones.

questions.prompt: A teammate on another machine needs your three-component setup. The directory sits in a repo you both have read access to, it will change every few weeks, and neither of you wants to maintain an install step. What is the smallest thing that works?
options: They clone the repo and run `claude --plugin-dir ./guardrail-kit` in each session themselves
They add your repo as a marketplace once, then install and update the plugin by name as it changes
You zip the plugin and send a new zip every time anything changes
They copy the plugin folder into their own `~/.claude/skills/` and update it with git pull
questions.explanation: A marketplace entry lists the plugin and where to fetch it; they add it once, and from then on `claude plugin install name@marketplace` plus an update flow handles every change — which is exactly the drift problem plugins exist to solve. `--plugin-dir` (A) makes them remember a flag per session and never picks up changes, so it recreates the manual step you were trying to remove. Repackaging a zip (C) makes you the update mechanism. Pulling into `~/.claude/skills/` (D) works mechanically and is a fine solo trick, but it puts an unmanaged copy of a versioned plugin outside any version tracking, and it hardcodes an assumption about where their plugins live.
